newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY LEAGUE-BRITISH CLUBS INCREASE OVERSEAS QUOTA.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY LEAGUE-BRITISH CLUBS INCREASE OVERSEAS QUOTA.

text.p: British professional clubs will be allowed to have six overseas players on their register for a two-year period starting next season, the Rugby Football League Council decided on Wednesday.
RFL chief executive Maurice Lindsay said: "We have a surplus of players available to Super League in Australia and this will enable British clubs to take up some of those players.

"This may help our clubs maintain their strength for the World Club Championship and in view of the continuing call by rugby union for some of our top players it would assist in maintaining the high standard of our club sides."
The Council, the professional game's ruling body, also ratified a blue-print for the unification of the game with the British Amateur Rugby League Association (BARLA).
Lindsay said: "Quite clearly rugby league as a sport will be unable to make any further substantial progress unless there is unification.
"There would be substantial grant aid available to the sport if we were unified and there are serious worries that we could lose whatever grants are given to the game unless we can join together.
"We are the last major sport in Britain to have two separate ruling bodies which oversee the amateur and professional aspects of their own sport.
"I'm very encouraged by what our clubs have done and just hope that the BARLA clubs will see things the same way."
The amateur clubs are expected to consider the plan in February although Lindsay hopes they will do so earlier.
